Article Title: Voluminous evidence in graft cases leading to long pendency: SC
Article Text:
Supreme Court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Flagging the issue of prosecuting agencies filing voluminous evidence and naming large number of witnesses in corruption cases, Supreme Court disapproved of the practice, saying it leads to protracted hearing and long pendency.While acquitting a person in a 33-year-old corruption case on the ground that CBI failed to prove that he received pecuniary advantage, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran expressed concern over the agency naming a large number of unnecessary witnesses to prove the charge.The court said voluminous documents filed by CBI are intimidating even to the court. "We cannot but notice that in corruption cases voluminous evidence is led, which is often intimidating to the court, especially since many aspects attempted to be led in evidence are way off the mark, in providing a substantiation of the allegation, or to bring home the guilt of the accused public servant," the bench said.The case pertains to a complaint filed by Assam veterinary department alleging that a loss of Rs 5.97 lakh was caused to the exchequer as payment was made to a fictitious firm for medicines which were never supplied. Seven persons were chargesheeted, of whom four were convicted and sentenced by a trial court and three acquitted.Three convicts filed an appeal before Gauhati high court. One of them, the accountant who passed the bill, was acquitted, but the petitioner, who was store in charge, and the other accused, storekeeper, were convicted under Section 13(1)(d) of Prevention of Corruption Act. The petitioner then moved SC. Allowing his appeal, the bench set aside his conviction and noted that the prosecution in this case had examined 62 witnesses, which was of no avail as the HC referred to only nine of such witnesses.
Article Summary: Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran expressed concern over the agency naming a large number of unnecessary witnesses to prove the charge. The court said voluminous documents filed by CBI are intimidating even to the court.

Article Title: Interim EC ruling on ‘real TMC’ likely on Sept 17
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An interesting situation may be unfolding in Nandigram and Rejinagar -- the two assembly seats in West Bengal set for bypolls on Oct 6 -- with both factions of Trinamool Congress, one led by Mamata Banerjee and the other by Ritabrata Banerjee, naming own candidates while claiming to be the "real" party entitled to use its reserved 'twin flower' symbol.The Election Commission , which had heard the two factions on their claims and counter-claims on Saturday, asked them to file written replies to each other's pleas staking claim to be the "real" TMC, by Sept 16. Interestingly, Sept 16 is also the last date for filing nomination for the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypoll.Sources indicated that EC may examine the replies and come up with an interim decision on Sept 17, the day when scrutiny of nominations will take place. This may or may not be preceded by an in-person hearing. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar is currently in Bhutan and returning by Sept 17 noon. A full commission meeting may thus have to wait till then.Given that the nominations would have been filed by the afternoon of Sept 16, with separate candidates fielded by each faction, the returning officer (RO) may need to adjudicate whether either candidates can contest under the party's reserved symbol and, if so, which one.The RO may escalate the file to the Election Commission of India through the West Bengal chief electoral officer, since EC is the authority to decide symbol disputes.Conventionally, EC freezes the party symbol in the event of an internal split and an imminent poll/bypoll, until final settlement of the dispute, and asks the rival factions to contest the poll under a new party name and symbol. The new symbol must be picked from the list of free symbols or can be of the party's own choosing.In the latest case relating to the TMC split, were the EC to issue an interim order on Sept 17 freezing the TMC symbol, the RO may allow candidates fielded by the rival groups, to contest under a different symbol. Technically, the symbols are allotted by RO to the candidates only after the last date for withdrawal of candidatures, which as per the current bypoll schedule is Sept 19.Since the rival factions would, as per the interim arrangement, need to pick new party names, there is a chance that the RO may require the rival factions' candidates to contest as independents. This is as nomination papers cannot be altered after the filing deadline.
Article Summary: Nandigram and Rejinagar, two assembly seats in West Bengal set for bypolls on Oct 6. Both factions of Trinamool Congress, one led by Mamata Banerjee, naming own candidates. Claim to be the "real" party entitled to use its reserved 'twin flower' symbol.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has ruled that if a person is convicted in two cases and sentenced separately, the period of imprisonment undergone as an undertrial can be offset against only one of the sentences and not both even when the trial court had ordered the two sentences to run concurrently.The ruling was given by a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta while detecting that gangster Abu Salem, who was extradited from Portugal in Nov 2005 on a solemn assurance by Indian govt that he would not be awarded death penalty or a jail term of more than 25 years, had computed his undertrial incarceration period twice to seek release from jail on the ground that he has already spent 25 years in jail, even though he was awarded life sentences in two terror cases in 2015 and 2017.Justice Nath said, "The fact that sentences imposed in the two cases were directed to run concurrently is of significance. Sentences granted concurrently operate simultaneously, hence the same period of incarceration cannot be notionally counted twice for the purpose of determining completion of the sentence.""The appellant (Salem) cannot treat the period preceding the later conviction as undertrial custody for one sentence while simultaneously treating the same period, from the date of the earlier conviction, as post-conviction custody for the other sentence and thereby secure a double benefit," Justice Nath said.SC said the sovereign commitment given to Portugal govt that no sentence extending beyond 25 years would be imposed upon Salem has no bearing on the judicial determination of Salem's guilt in two terror cases and award of life sentences."Prescription of the nature and extent of punishment is governed by the Legislature and its application to the facts of a particular case falls within the domain of the Judiciary. The Executive, in turn, exercises such powers in relation to remission, commutation or release as are conferred upon it by law," it said.SC referred to the govt affidavit which had categorised Salem among prisoners who have been sentenced to 50 years of imprisonment. After reducing the set-off and remission periods, it had informed SC that the probable date of Salem's release would be Jan 31, 2046, that is, after another 20 years.Dismissing Salem's appeal, SC said the calculations carried out by govt indicate that he continues to serve life sentence and "the stipulation that he cannot be detained beyond 25 years is a consequence of the sovereign assurance extended by Union govt to Portugal's govt. It does not convert sentence of life imprisonment into a fixed-term sentence of 25 years".
Article Summary: Abu Salem was extradited from Portugal in Nov 2005 on a solemn assurance by Indian govt that he would not be awarded death penalty or a jail term of more than 25 years. Salem had computed his undertrial incarceration period twice to seek release from jail on the ground that he has already spent 25 years in jail.

NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule on Monday questioned the registration of a CBI FIR into the death of Disha Salian, saying she was surprised because the case had earlier been treated as closed by the same government.Salian, a former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput , died after falling from the 12th floor of a building in Mumbai’s Malad area on June 8, 2020. The CBI registered an FIR on September 13 following a direction from the Bombay High Court for a fresh probe into the circumstances surrounding her death.“I was surprised to hear how this (registration of an FIR by CBI) happened because it is the same government that had closed the case. I do not understand what is happening,” Sule told reporters in Pune.She said she would speak to Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut to understand the latest developments.According to CBI officials cited by news agency PTI, the FIR does not name any individual as an accused, in line with the Bombay High Court’s directions. It invokes IPC provisions relating to criminal conspiracy, gang rape, murder, disappearance of evidence and public servants allegedly framing incorrect records.The FIR followed a September 2 order by the Bombay High Court on a petition filed by Salian’s father, Satish Salian. The CBI began recording statements after the court directed it to conduct a thorough investigation.The court had criticised the Mumbai Police investigation, noting “glaring discrepancies” and observing that the probe “raises more questions than answers”.It had also directed that nobody should be treated as an accused unless investigators found sufficient grounds for reasonable suspicion based on the material collected during the probe.Advocate Nilesh Ojha, who represents Satish Salian, claimed on Monday that the FIR contains the names of several individuals, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray , Rohan Roy, Rhea Chakraborty, Param Bir Singh, Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, among others.However, the CBI has not publicly confirmed the names claimed by the advocate, according to PTI.Ojha said the FIR was registered after the CBI conducted preliminary verification of Satish Salian’s complaint and recorded his statement. He said the case covers allegations of gang rape, murder and an alleged cover-up, invoking IPC Sections 376D, 302, 201, 217, 218 and 120B.Satish Salian had earlier approached the court alleging that his daughter was murdered.Speaking to news agency ANI on Friday, he said he had provided investigators with the names of people whom he wanted examined.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down,” he said.Asked whether she saw a possible political conspiracy behind the development, Sule did not give a direct answer.“Anything is possible,” she said, while referring to what she called “ICE” — Income Tax, CBI and Enforcement Directorate — and alleging that central agencies had previously been used against political figures who later joined the ruling party.AIMIM leader Waris Pathan, meanwhile, said the case should not be politicised and should be left to the courts.“There is no need to give the Disha Salian case a political colour. There is no need to politicise it,” Pathan said, adding that the matter was sub judice and that “it is best to let the court decide”.Salian’s death had earlier been recorded as an Accidental Death Report. The Bombay High Court had raised concerns over the fact that no FIR was registered despite allegations by her family that she had been murdered.The court also noted that copies of the post-mortem report and ADR had not been provided to her family for years.Sushant Singh Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence six days after Salian’s death.The CBI later submitted a closure report in Rajput’s case, concluding that he died by suicide; that report remains pending before the competent court.The Bombay High Court has directed the CBI to investigate the Salian case and has left it to the agency to determine whether a criminal case is made out based on the evidence collected.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule questioned the registration of a CBI FIR into the death of Disha Salian. She said she was surprised because the case had earlier been treated as closed by the same government. AIMIM leader Waris Pathan said the case should not be politicised and should be left to the courts.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday thanked the people of Rajasthan after the BJP emerged as the largest party in the state’s municipal elections, winning more wards than the Congress and securing majorities in four of the 10 municipal corporations.In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJP’s policies of development and good governance under the “double-engine government”.“Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections,” PM Modi wrote.“This is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),” he added.PM Modi also congratulated the winning candidates and BJP workers, saying the mandate would strengthen the party’s resolve to work towards development and prosperity in the state.According to figures from the Rajasthan State Election Commission, results for 10,235 of the state’s 10,244 wards had been declared by 8.30 pm on Monday.The BJP had won 4,179 wards compared with 3,613 for the Congress. The BJP crossed the majority mark in Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota and Bhilwara municipal corporations, while the Congress secured a majority in Bikaner.The Congress also recorded a major victory in the Jhalawar municipal council, considered a stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.The elections covered 309 urban local bodies — 10 municipal corporations, 47 municipal councils and 252 municipal boards.In Kota Municipal Corporation, the BJP secured 55 of the 100 wards, while Congress won 40 and Independents three. The result for Ward 87 was put on hold after an EVM malfunction.Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma and other party workers staged a protest outside the counting centre, seeking the result and alleging irregularities.Officials later sealed the machine in the presence of the district collector and additional district magistrate and forwarded a report to the Election Commission through the returning officer.The BJP also retained several individual seats. Vivek Rajvanshi won his fourth consecutive term from Ward 54, defeating Congress candidate Manish by 2,226 votes.Gopal Ram Manda secured his fifth consecutive election victory, defeating Congress candidate Sanjay Yadav by 899 votes.Congress and Independent candidates, however, registered victories in some key wards. Youth Congress candidate Arpit Jain defeated BJP veteran and former deputy mayor Yogendra Khinchi by 250 votes in Ward 86.Independent candidate Vandana Faujdar won Ward 71 with 1,264 votes, defeating BJP candidate Meenakshi Sen by 160 votes.In Bundi, the BJP initially emerged as the largest party with 29 wards, two short of a majority. Congress won 20 wards, while Independents secured 11.Later in the day, three Independent candidates, Prabhat Devi, Aatmaram Chopdar and Vishal Sharma, joined the BJP, taking the party to a majority and enabling it to form the board.The BJP had also captured the previous mid-term board after Congress council chairperson Madu Nuwal was suspended.Congress leaders had expected to retain control but faced criticism over ticket distribution. Former councillors Devraj Gochar, Ankit Buliwal and Jeeshan Ali, who were denied Congress tickets, won as Independents.BJP president Nitin Nabin thanked Rajasthan voters for what he described as a “historic victory”, saying the results showed continued faith in Modi’s leadership.BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also cited the party’s performance in Kota, where Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had conducted the student-centric programme ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’.“In Kota, where Rahul Gandhi had gone and attempted to create ‘jhooth ki goonj’, the BJP appears to be winning spectacularly,” Trivedi said.He claimed the results demonstrated that the Congress had “more propaganda and less reality” in its claims.

DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday reviewed the functioning of the CM Helpline 1905 at the Secretariat and directed officials to ensure the swift, time-bound and satisfactory resolution of public grievances.The chief minister said that the CM Helpline is an important mechanism for addressing the problems of the common people. He stressed that grievance redressal should not be limited to formally closing complaints on the portal, but must ensure an actual resolution of the complainant's problem.Dhami directed district magistrates to review complaints department-wise in districts where a particular category of grievances is being received in large numbers and ensure their early resolution. He also called for an analysis of the reasons behind repeated complaints of the same nature and effective measures to address such issues permanently.The chief minister directed all district magistrates to conduct surprise inspections of tehsils. During these inspections, special attention should be paid to whether mutation-related cases are being disposed of within the prescribed timelines. He said complaints related to land fraud should be addressed on priority. The chief minister stressed that people should not be made to make unnecessary visits to government offices for revenue-related matters and that prescribed services must be delivered within the stipulated timeDhami directed officials to accord top priority to ensuring the availability of clean drinking water.He said complaints related to drinking water should be acted upon immediately. He directed the concerned officials to conduct an audit of water pipelines and sewer lines within 15 days and submit a report. Timely resolution of disruptions in water supply, leakages and other related issues should be ensured.The chief minister directed officials to pay special attention to grievances pending for more than 30 days. Secretaries, heads of departments and district magistrates should regularly review pending complaints at their respective levels. Accountability should be fixed for officials in cases where complaints are not resolved within the prescribed timeframe.He further directed that long-pending complaints be resolved on the highest priority. During the meeting, a department-wise status of complaints pending for more than 180 days was also presented. Dhami said such old cases should be regularly monitored at the departmental level and the reasons for their pendency should also be reviewed.The chief minister instructed officials not to close complaints unnecessarily under "Special Close" or "Force Close" categories. He said the satisfaction of complainants must be given due importance in grievance redressal. Before closing any complaint, officials must ensure that all necessary action has been taken at the appropriate level to resolve the issue.Dhami said the feedback mechanism for complaints received through the CM Helpline should be further strengthened. The quality of grievance redressal should be assessed on the basis of feedback received from complainants. The portal has provisions for obtaining public feedback and monitoring the action being taken by various departments and nodal officers.The chief minister said officials and personnel performing well in grievance redressal should be encouraged, while accountability should be fixed for those found guilty of unnecessary delays or negligence. He said the fundamental objective of the CM Helpline is to establish effective communication between the government and the public and ensure real, time-bound and satisfactory resolution of citizens' problems.During the review, the chief minister also spoke to several complainants over the phone to ascertain the actual status of their grievances and their redressal.Dhami spoke to Sanjay Kumar Rawat regarding a complaint that had been closed inappropriately. Rawat informed him that medical reimbursement bills related to the treatment of his late father had not been paid. The chief minister directed the concerned officials to take immediate necessary action and ensure payment of the pending medical reimbursement. He said people should not be unnecessarily harassed in such sensitive cases and warned that accountability would be fixed if similar complaints arise in the future.The chief minister also spoke to Baby Kotnala, a resident of Pauri Garhwal, regarding her issue related to destitute women's pension. She informed him that despite registering a complaint a long time ago, the issue had not been resolved. Dhami directed the District Magistrate, Pauri Garhwal, to take immediate appropriate action and ensure resolution of the matter.Dhami also spoke to Haridwar resident Geeta, who informed him that a water tank had been constructed near her house around three months ago, but water supply from the tank had not yet commenced. The chief minister directed the chief development officer, Haridwar, to inspect the site and ensure immediate commencement of the water supply.The chief minister spoke to Dehradun resident Shilpi Saxena, who informed him that a streetlight had been installed in her area within the stipulated timeframe after she lodged a complaint on the CM Helpline. She thanked the chief minister for resolving the issue.Similarly, Almora resident Ayush Bisht informed the chief minister that his complaint related to a scholarship had been resolved by the department. Dhami directed officials to investigate the reasons for the delay in disbursing the scholarship and said students must receive the benefits of government schemes within the prescribed timeframe.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday reviewed the functioning of the CM Helpline 1905 at the Secretariat. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Monday said his government adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards gangsters, extortionists, drug traffickers and organised criminal networks, irrespective of how powerful or well-connected they may claim to be.He further asserted that law and order is fully maintained in Punjab and there is no haven for criminals.Felicitating the Punjab Police team led by Superintendent of Police, Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF), Bikramjit Singh Brar, for securing the extradition of notorious fugitive criminal Amritpal Singh alias Amrit Dalam from the Republic of Moldova, the chief minister said the government is fully committed to Punjab's peace and security.Dalam was detained by the Moldovan authorities on February 24 while trying to cross the Otaci state border to Ukraine. Subsequently, the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC) of the Punjab Police began an extradition process to bring him to India.Mann highlighted that 1,234 gangster modules have been busted and 10 fugitives deported from abroad, while 60,582 FIRs have been registered against drug traffickers and properties worth Rs 366 crore seized.He highlighted that the Punjab Police is equipped with high-tech anti-drone systems and Village Defence Committees comprising 1.5 lakh people have been formed, warning that no person or group attempting to disturb Punjab's peace will be spared.Felicitating the police officers for their exemplary achievement, Mann said, "The successful extradition sends an unequivocal message to gangsters, criminals and their handlers operating from foreign soil that Punjab Police will chase them across borders and bring them back to face the law."Gangsters cannot find a haven for themselves anymore. Whether they are hiding in Punjab, another part of India or thousands of kilometres away in Europe, the Punjab Police will track them down. They may change their locations, passports and identities, but they cannot escape the law forever, the chief minister said.Extradition of Amrit Dalam is a major achievement in Punjab's relentless campaign against organised crime and demonstrates the effectiveness of the state government's 'Gangstran Te Vaar' campaign, Mann stated."Amrit Dalam was a key operative of the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria Gang and was wanted in several serious criminal cases, including murder, attempt to murder, offences under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, Arms Act and narcotic offence," he added.Mann appreciated the coordinated efforts of the GTF, Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC), Punjab Police and central agencies, saying that close inter-agency coordination has emerged as a powerful weapon in dismantling transnational criminal networks.During its recent visit to Moldova, the Punjab Police team received a token of appreciation from the government of the Republic of Moldova in recognition of the close coordination and cooperation that facilitated the first-ever extradition of a fugitive criminal from Moldova to India.Describing the gesture as a matter of pride for Punjab, Mann said, "This recognition reflects the mutual trust, respect and growing law-enforcement cooperation between India and Moldova. NEW DELHI: The civil aviation ministry has issued a show-cause notice to Air India over alleged procedural lapses that allowed three Italian passengers to board a connecting flight from Delhi without completing immigration formalities earlier this month.The notice has been issued to the Air India CEO.The home ministry has also convened a meeting of stakeholders on Tuesday to discuss the incident, sources told news agency PTI.The three passengers flew from Amritsar to Delhi on September 4 before boarding a Lufthansa flight to Munich from Delhi airport. However, they did not complete the required immigration formalities at the airport, sources added.Titled “violation of SOP for hub and spoke operations resulting in three foreign nationals departing India without mandatory immigration clearance,” the show-cause notice issued to Air India last Saturday said the three passengers arrived in Delhi from Amritsar on AI 1115 at 12.50 am on September 4 and subsequently departed for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight at 1.45 am, within an hour of their arrival.Home secretary Govind Mohan will chair a meeting on Tuesday to discuss the incident.The secretary and additional secretary of the civil aviation ministry, Intelligence Bureau director, additional secretary (UT and Foreigners) of the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration commissioner, Air India CEO and Delhi airport CEO are expected to attend the meeting, they added.Amritsar airport is among the airports where Air India operates flights under its ‘Hub-and-Spoke’ model.Under this arrangement, passengers complete immigration formalities at the airport of origin and can then travel to an overseas destination through a designated hub. At the hub airport, where the international flight departs, passengers are required only to undergo security checks before boarding.For a passenger travelling from Amritsar via Delhi to an international destination, Amritsar serves as the spoke and Delhi as the hub.In the case of the three Italian passengers, sources said they were issued boarding passes at Amritsar for both their flight to Delhi and the Lufthansa flight to Munich.However, as the two flights were not covered under Air India’s ‘Hub-and-Spoke’ model, the passengers were required to exit through the arrival area at Delhi and complete immigration formalities before taking the Lufthansa flight.After arriving at Delhi airport, they were instead taken to the international transfer area and did not reach the immigration counter. They then boarded the flight to Munich without completing the immigration process, the sources said, as cited by PTI.Air India and Lufthansa have an interline partnership. An interline agreement generally allows passengers to book connecting flights operated by different airlines under a single itinerary.
Article Summary: The three passengers flew from Amritsar to Delhi on September 4 before boarding a Lufthansa flight to Munich from Delhi airport. They did not complete the required immigration formalities at the airport, sources added. The home ministry has also convened a meeting of stakeholders on Tuesday to discuss the incident.

Nearly 50 lakh people across 15 districts of Bihar have been affected by floods as heavy rain in recent days caused rivers already flowing above danger levels to swell further, officials said on Monday.Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month, about six per cent above normal, according to the local weather office.According to the Disaster Management Department, floods have affected 49.67 lakh people across 15 districts in Bihar.The affected districts include Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria.An official said incessant rain in the catchment areas of rivers flowing from Nepal into Bihar, along with heavy rainfall in the state, has pushed several rivers and streams above their danger marks, as cited by PTI.The Ganga was flowing at 36.19 metres at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur at 6.00 pm on Monday, 1.69 metres above the danger level.The Kosi river was flowing above the danger mark at Baltara and Kursela, while the Budhi Gandak had crossed the danger level at Khagaria.The Ganga was above the danger mark at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger. The Punpun at Sripalpur, Bagmati at Benibad and Ghaghara at Darauli were also flowing above their respective danger levels.The administration has set up 1,248 community kitchens and 13 relief camps in the flood-hit areas. Around 11,508 people have been provided accommodation, food, medical care and other essential facilities, officials said.The Disaster Management Department said the Gandak barrage at Valmiki Nagar recorded a water discharge of 1,09,000 cusecs at 4 pm on Monday, with the flow continuing to rise.At the Kosi Barrage in Birpur, the discharge stood at 1,63,315 cusecs, against this year's highest flow of 2,55,425 cusecs recorded on July 20.Twenty-seven teams of the State Disaster Response Force and 10 teams of the National Disaster Response Force have been deployed across various districts for relief and rescue operations.
Article Summary: Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month, about six per cent above normal. The affected districts include Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai and Munger.

Article Title: ‘Partners, not rivals’: China FM Wang Yi reveals key PM Modi-Xi consensus

18th BRICS Summit in Delhi

NEW DELHI: India and China should view each other as partners rather than rivals, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi said on Monday, citing the consensus reached between president Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi.Wang said the two leaders held a “candid and in-depth exchange of views” on strategic and long-term issues concerning bilateral ties, according to news agency PTI. “The most important consensus they reached was that China and India should be partners,” he told Chinese official media.According to Wang, Xi said China and India could draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed and pursue common development. The two leaders also agreed to maintain peace and tranquillity in border areas and support each other during their respective BRICS chairmanships.The Chinese foreign ministry said the relationship had moved from a “restart” to a “renewed elevation” under the strategic guidance of the two leaders. Wang said areas of cooperation were expanding, trade had reached record levels and people-to-people exchanges were becoming more active.Wang also quoted PM Modi as saying India was ready to be “a partner, not an adversary” to China and viewed each other’s development “as an opportunity rather than a challenge”. He said PM had reaffirmed that India’s approach to China was independent of third-party influence.The two leaders, according to Wang, agreed to deepen political trust, appropriately manage differences and strengthen cooperation in areas including cultural exchanges and direct air connectivity. They also agreed to coordinate more closely through the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and the G20, while advancing cooperation among Global South countries.The Indian foreign ministry’s account of the meeting highlighted the need for a “strategic and long-term perspective” in managing bilateral ties. According to MEA, PM Modi said differences should not become disputes and that relations should be guided by “three mutuals” — mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.PM Modi also stressed that peace and tranquillity along the border remained essential for the broader relationship and called for adherence to existing agreements and understandings. Both sides backed a “fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution” of the boundary question.On trade, the leaders discussed structural imbalances, supply-chain concerns and the need for “meaningful and predictable market access”. They also welcomed progress in people-to-people ties and called for greater cultural, business and travel links.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing would work with New Delhi to implement the understandings reached by the leaders and “make the cooperation list longer”.She said, "As the two leaders have charted the course for the future development of the bilateral ties, China will work with India to implement the important common understandings reached between the two leaders."With China set to assume the BRICS chairmanship in 2027, both sides are expected to build on the latest engagement.
Article Summary: China and India should view each other as partners rather than rivals, Chinese foreign minister says. Wang Yi cites consensus reached between president Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Xi said China and India could draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed.

Article Title: UCC in Bihar? JD(U) opposes implementation despite backing Bill in Parliament
Article Text:
Former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar

NEW DELHI: Senior JD(U) leader Shyam Rajak on Monday said the party was opposed to implementing the Uniform Civil Code in Bihar , despite having "supported the UCC Bill" in Parliament.The former JD(U) national general secretary said the party's position on the issue had been clearly articulated by its supreme leader and former chief minister Nitish Kumar "Our stand on the issue was made clear by our leader way back. He had said that although our party was supporting the UCC Bill in the Parliament, it was not in favour of implementing the same in Bihar," Rajak said.When asked whether the JD(U)'s position would have little significance with Nitish Kumar stepping down and BJP leader Samrat Choudhary becoming the new chief minister, Rajak strongly rejected the suggestion."The chief minister may be of the BJP but the government is being run with the help of allies... our stand is clear, the question of implementing UCC in Bihar does not arise," he said.When approached for a comment, JD(U) legislature party leader and minister Shrawon Kumar said, "This is an issue on which our spokespersons shall speak. I would like to hear what they say, and then I will say more."Meanwhile, JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha on Monday said party leaders would soon meet Union Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code in states.“We will soon meet Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the issue,” Jha told news agency PTI.With 12 Lok Sabha MPs, the JD(U) is a key constituent of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and shares power with the BJP in Bihar.The development comes a day after Shah asserted that NDA governments in 21 states would introduce UCC before 2029.Addressing a press conference in Mumbai on Sunday, Shah highlighted the government's initiatives for women and said, “Triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. We have introduced UCC in several states, and I am confident that in the 21 BJP-NDA ruled states, we will introduce the UCC before 2029.”The press conference was held to announce a month-long campaign beginning September 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 76th birthday and 25 years of his public service, which began with his tenure as Gujarat chief minister.
Article Summary: Senior JD(U) leader Shyam Rajak on Monday said the party was opposed to implementing the Uniform Civil Code in Bihar. Rajak strongly rejected the suggestion that the party's position would have little significance with Nitish Kumar stepping down and BJP leader Samrat Choudhary becoming the new chief minister.
